transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello Doctor. It's, uh, very nice to meet you. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. 

I'm really only here because... well, my family and everyone else says I’ve been doing too much lately. I certainly don't want to cause a fuss or worry anyone, so I agreed to come in and talk to you. I want to do the right thing.

But honestly, to me, it just feels like I’m the only one with enough drive to actually get things done. Is it so wrong to want to be productive? I mean, we have this big move coming up, and I've been making sure to get the move handled, plus I need to rebuild the new garage right so it's sturdy—if you don't do it yourself, it doesn't get done right, you know? And I've been organizing things down at the church, and... well, I'm still running the grinders at the plant, trying to show the younger fellows at work how the job actually ought to be done. 

I just like being helpful and staying on top of things. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Do you ever feel like you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to focus on something else?

Well, Doctor... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer here. But no, I don't think I have anything quite like that. 

I mean, sure, I'm thinking about the garage and the move a lot, but they don't just repeat in my head against my will when I'm trying to do something else. When I'm at the plant, I'm focused on the grinders, and when I'm at the church, I'm focused on that. My mind feels very clear, actually. 

I hope I'm understanding your question right? I just wouldn't say I get stuck on thoughts like that. Am I explaining that okay for you?
Do you feel like things need to be done perfectly, or that if they're not done a certain way, they're not done right?

Well, I... I wouldn't say "perfectly." I don't want to sound like I'm some sort of control freak or anything like that. I just... well, I have a lot of experience, you know? At my age, you learn how things ought to be done so they last. 

Like with the garage, or down at the plant with the grinders. I just want to make sure the younger guys learn the right way to do it so nobody gets hurt and the job gets done right. I don't think that's being too particular, do you? I just like to be thorough and helpful. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I certainly don't mean to come across as difficult or anything.
Do you find it hard to let others handle tasks or projects without getting involved yourself?

Well, I... I suppose I do like to be involved, yes. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm trying to be bossy or anything. It's just that, well, I have the energy for it right now, and I want to be useful. 

If I see something that needs doing, like the organizing at the church, I just naturally step in to help out. I don't want anyone else to have to carry the load if I can do it, you know? It's not that I can't let them do it, I just... I want to make things easier for everyone. 

Is that alright? I just try to be a good neighbor and a hard worker. I hope I'm not doing something wrong by wanting to pitch in.
Do you ever find time to relax or engage in activities that you enjoy, unrelated to work or helping others?

Well, Doctor, I... I suppose I don't do a whole lot of just sitting around right now. I hope that's okay to say. I know folks my age are supposed to be taking it easy and playing golf or something, but... well, I just feel so good, you know? 

I mean, I enjoy the work. Getting the garage ready for the move, helping out down at the plant, organizing things at the church... that *is* what I enjoy. It makes me feel alive and useful. I don't really need to sit in a recliner to relax when I've got all this energy. 

I hope that doesn't sound strange? I just don't want you to think I'm running myself ragged. I feel better than I have in years, honestly. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Do you worry that if you don't do something yourself, it won't be done correctly?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I worry about it, exactly. I don't want you to think I'm sitting around fretting over every little thing or not trusting people. That's not me at all. 

It's more just... well, like I said before, I have a certain way of doing things that I know works, especially with the machinery at the plant or, you know, packing up the garage. I just prefer to handle it so I know it's safe and secure. It's just being responsible, really. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound stubborn or anything? I just like to be helpful and make sure things are done right the first time so nobody else has to go back and fix it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I really want to make sure I'm giving you good answers.
Do you have trouble delegating tasks to others when you're in charge of a project?

Well, I... I guess I don't really see myself as being "in charge" of things, usually. I'm just a guy who likes to pitch in, you know? 

But, um, I suppose if I am the one leading something, I don't mind asking for help if I really need it. I hope that's the right answer? I just... I don't want to come across like I'm hoarding all the work or refusing to let folks help. It's just that, right now, with all this energy I have, it's often just quicker for me to do it myself than to explain it to someone else. 

I'm not trying to be difficult, I promise. I just want things to go smoothly for everyone. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm being helpful.
Do you often find yourself correcting others or telling them how to do things, even when they don't ask for your opinion?

Oh, gosh, no. I... I really try not to be one of those people. You know, an older fellow poking his nose where it doesn't belong. I hope I don't ever come across that way to anyone. 

If one of the younger guys at the plant asks me how to set the blending mix or run the grinder, well, sure, I'm happy to show them the ropes. But just walking up and telling folks they're doing it wrong when they didn't ask? No, I don't think I do that at all. I really try to be polite and mind my own business. 

I hope that's a good thing? I don't want you to think I'm ignoring people who might need a hand, I just... I want to make sure I'm being respectful of everyone's toes, so to speak. Am I answering that right for you, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you ever feel like you're unable to stop yourself from getting involved in tasks or projects, even when you know you should probably let someone else handle them?

Well, I... I try my best to know my limits. I really do. I don't want to be a bother to anyone or step on toes, like I was saying. 

I guess... well, lately, since I've been feeling so, you know, fired up and ready to go, I might jump into things a little quicker than usual. Like at the plant, if I see a batch getting backed up, I might just hop on the line and start clearing it out before the supervisor even says anything. But I wouldn't say I can't stop myself. It's more just... wanting to be useful, you know? Pitching in where I see a need. 

I really hope that doesn't sound like I'm out of control or anything. I just like to be a hard worker. Is that... is that okay? I'm not trying to make trouble for anyone, I just want to be a good help. Am I doing alright with these questions, Doctor?
Do you feel anxious or uncomfortable when things are not done according to your plans or expectations?

Well, I... I really hate to admit this part, Doctor. I try so hard to be easygoing, I really do. But, um... lately, I guess I have been getting a little, well, impatient. 

I hope you don't think less of me for saying it, but I've just been feeling lately like everybody needs to either get on board with my plans or just... get out of my way. It's confusing, honestly, because one minute I'm joking around, feeling ten feet tall and just on top of the world, and then the next minute I'm snapping at my wife, or my boy, over some little question they ask me. 

I always feel just awful about it afterward. I really don't want to be short with my family, they don't deserve that. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding like a terrible husband or father, I just... I want to make sure I'm being honest and giving you the right answers. Am I doing okay?
Do you have any recurring thoughts or images that disturb you or make you feel anxious?

Oh, no, no. I don't think so. I mean, I try to keep my mind on the positive things, you know? The good Lord has given me a lot to be thankful for, and I try to focus on that. 

I wouldn't say I have any... any disturbing pictures in my head or anything like that. My mind does race a bit lately, like I mentioned, just thinking about all the things I want to get done at the house and the plant. But it's not scary thoughts, just... busy thoughts. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer. I don't want to leave anything out if it's important, but I really don't think I have those kinds of bad thoughts. Is that what you were looking for, Doctor? I just want to be sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Do you have trouble getting rid of things you no longer need or use?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I like to keep a tidy house, and my wife and I usually do a good job of clearing out the clutter when spring rolls around. 

I mean, I might hold onto a few extra parts or tools out in the garage, just in case something breaks down and I need to fix it in a pinch. You never know when a spare bolt or a piece of wire might come in handy, right? But I wouldn't say I have trouble getting rid of things. If it's truly garbage, it goes in the bin. 

I try not to be one of those folks who just hoards everything. I hope that's the kind of answer you need. I'm trying my best to be helpful, Doctor. Am I answering everything okay for you today?
Do you ever feel like you're doing things without fully thinking them through?

Well, I... I guess maybe a little bit lately. I try to be responsible, Doctor, I really do. I've always been a good provider, and I like to make sure everything is taken care of. 

But, um... I suppose I have made a few decisions recently that... well, that I didn't exactly run by my wife first. I just felt so sure about them at the time, you know? Like, I went ahead and put down some deposits for work on the garage, and bought some new equipment. It just seemed like the perfect time to get it all done, but... well, she wasn't too happy that we hadn't talked it over. I feel terrible about upsetting her. 

And I guess I've been rushing around a lot, too. Driving back and forth between the houses, trying to get everything done at once. And at the plant, I've been pushing to get jobs finished real quick. A few of the fellas there even told me I was taking chances, rushing like that. I didn't mean to be reckless, I just... I had so much energy and it felt like I could handle it all. 

I hope you don't think I'm being foolish, Doctor. I'm usually very careful. I just... I got a little carried away, I suppose. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find it hard to control your impulses and behaviors when you're excited or stressed?

Well, I... I don't think I lose control, no. I mean, even with the things I just mentioned about the garage and rushing around, I always felt like I was the one in the driver's seat, you know? Just... maybe driving a little faster than usual. 

But I wouldn't say I can't control myself. Working around the heavy mixers and grinders at the plant all these years, you really learn to keep a steady hand, even when things get stressful or busy. You have to be disciplined, and I've always prided myself on being a reliable guy. I don't just fly off the handle or do things I can't stop myself from doing. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm making excuses for upsetting my wife earlier. I just want you to know that I'm usually very level-headed. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Do you ever feel like you're acting on your impulses without fully considering the consequences?

Well, no, sir... I really don't think so. I mean, even when I made those quick decisions about the garage that I mentioned, I honestly felt like I had thought it all through. I thought it was a wonderful plan at the time, you know? I always try to keep my family's best interests at heart. 

I don't just... jump into things completely blind. Like I said, working with the heavy mixers and equipment at the plant for so long, you get used to looking ahead and being careful. So I wouldn't say I ignore the consequences at all. I really do try very hard to do the right thing and be responsible. 

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, Doctor. I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I operate. Is this what you're looking for? I want to make sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time making sure every little detail is just right?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I'm overly fussy about every little detail, no. I mean, I like to do a good job, of course. At the plant, you have to make sure the mix is right, so I'm used to paying attention to what I'm doing. 

But I don't get bogged down in it, you know? I don't spend hours agonizing over tiny things. I just try to be thorough and do my work properly, like any responsible person would. I like things to be neat, but I wouldn't say I obsess over it. 

I hope that's alright, Doctor. I just want to be honest with you. Am I explaining that well enough? I want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Do you often find yourself double-checking your work to make sure everything is accurate?

Well, no, sir, not really. I mean, I'll give things a standard look-over, just to be sure I didn't make a silly mistake. When you've been working the mixing machines as long as I have, you just sort of know when the blend is correct. You don't need to keep going back to check it over and over again. 

I just try to do it the right way the first time. I don't want you to think I'm careless, though! I'm very diligent with my work, and I take a lot of pride in that. I just don't have that urge to keep checking the same thing repeatedly once I know it's done right. 

I hope I'm being helpful here. Is that the sort of detail you were looking for, Doctor? I just want to make sure we're on the same page and that I'm giving you good answers.
Do you feel like you can easily stop an activity when you want to, or do you find it hard to quit once you've started?

Well, sir, I'd say I can stop whenever I need to. I don't really have a problem putting things down. 

I mean, if I'm working on a project around the house, or back when I was running the mixers at the plant... when it's time to take a break or call it a day, I just stop. I don't get, you know, stuck on doing one thing for hours on end if I'm not supposed to. I like to think I'm pretty reasonable about knowing when it's time to quit and move on to something else. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information, Doctor. Am I doing okay with these questions so far?
Do you hold onto items because you think they might be useful someday or because they hold sentimental value?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I keep a few things, sure, but nothing out of the ordinary. 

My wife might say I have a few too many old tools in the garage, but they're just things I know I'll use to fix up the house. I don't just keep junk around for no reason, if that's what you mean. I like a tidy space, and I certainly don't let things pile up. I just hold onto the sensible things, you know, things a man ought to have around just in case. 

I don't want you to think I'm one of those people who can't throw a newspaper away! I'm very organized. I hope that's the right answer, Doctor. I'm trying my best to give you a clear picture of how I do things. Am I being helpful?
Do you feel a strong need to follow a specific routine or order in your daily activities?

Well, no, sir, I wouldn't say I have a strong need for it. I mean, I like things to be orderly, sure. Most folks my age do, I think. 

I wake up, have my coffee, read a bit... it's just a comfortable way to live. But I don't get upset if things change. If my wife wants to run an errand in the morning instead of the afternoon, well, that's just fine by me. I just like to know what's coming, but I don't force anyone to do things my way. I try to be very easygoing about it all. 

I don't want to sound rigid or anything like that. I'm very flexible, really. Does that sound like what you were asking about, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong impression of how I spend my days.
